unit.title: Executable Graph Invariants: A Deterministic Topological Sort
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student building production-oriented software-engineering habits
prerequisites: basic proof by induction or loop-invariant reasoning
learning_objectives: turn an algorithmic idea into a precise public contract
implement deterministic topological sorting with explicit failure behavior
justify partial correctness, termination, and cycle detection with invariants
test semantic properties and boundary cases using only the Python standard library
unit.completion_claim_limit: Completing this unit establishes evidence only for this kickoff unit, not for MIT 6.042J or any whole course.

required_evidence: the submitted module imports successfully in the designated Python environment
the engineering note contains a reviewable invariant argument, termination argument, complexity analysis, and contract discussion
completion_policy.validator_authority: Only the worker-harness-controlled validator may promote the job or unit result to SUCCEEDED.
completion_policy.unit_completion: Awarded only after independent evaluation of all required evidence; file presence or prose claims alone are insufficient.
completion_policy.course_completion: Never awarded by this unit. Later units and their separately validated evidence are required before any course-level completion decision.

provenance.authorship_note: The catalog identifies the course and public website pointers. The kickoff topic, task, and assessment design are course-manager-authored and are not represented as MIT-authored materials or an official MIT sequence.
